findings.detail: The full-screen loop called keypad() but never mousemask(), so the terminal never delivered wheel events and the transcript could only be moved with PgUp/PgDn. The loop now requests BUTTON4/BUTTON5 report support; a failed or unavailable mask is non-fatal.

read_key() passed a non-ASCII integer code through unchanged, but did not consume the queued curses mouse event. It now maps KEY_MOUSE to (mouse, bstate) through curses.getmouse() and leaves ordinary keys unchanged.

Wheel-up (BUTTON4_PRESSED) now scrolls one line toward older transcript rows and wheel-down (BUTTON5_PRESSED) scrolls one line toward latest. A mouse event with neither wheel bit is ignored, so enabling mouse reporting does not turn ordinary clicks into scrolling.

reviewed_evidence: Approval: product issue #35 is reachable from the repository and records the user bug report, exact baseline, branch and six-path write scope before this development branch is integrated.
Root cause: pocketchat/curses_ui.py had no mousemask() call or KEY_MOUSE/getmouse() path. The only transcript movement was KEY_PPAGE/KEY_NPAGE, so a terminal wheel could not reach the renderer.
Red tests observed before implementation: the wheel action left transcript_offset at 0, the KEY_MOUSE read path returned 409 instead of a mouse action, and the loop never called mousemask().

Implemented the smallest change in pocketchat/curses_ui.py: request BUTTON4_PRESSED|BUTTON5_PRESSED, convert KEY_MOUSE into (mouse, bstate), and map up/down to one-line scroll_transcript calls. No picker, click, paging or editor behavior changed.

Real PTY probe on macOS with TERM=xterm-256color: mousemask=2162688; injected XTerm wheel-up encoding produced curses mouse state=65536 (BUTTON4_PRESSED), x=9 y=4. This verifies event delivery at the curses boundary, not a human wheel gesture in every terminal.
unverified_scope: Only local macOS CPython 3.13.9 was run. Python 3.9, Linux, Windows (including no-curses fallback), exact-SHA GitHub Actions, package build, wheel, clean install, real provider and publication were not run. The PTY probe injected an XTerm wheel byte sequence; it does not prove every terminal, terminal multiplexer or OS reports the same encoding. Mouse clicks in the picker or editor remain unsupported by design.
